facts.statement: Crittendenceratops krzyzanowskii is the first dinosaur species formally named from the Fort Crittenden Formation.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, C. krzyzanowskii, and represents the first dinosaur taxon from that formation to receive a formal scientific name.

facts.statement: This dinosaur lived during the late Campanian period in the Fort Crittenden Formation of Arizona.
facts.quote: Crittendenceratops (meaning "horned face from the Fort Crittenden Formation") is a genus of horned centrosaurine ceratopsid dinosaur from the late Campanian Fort Crittenden Formation of Arizona.

facts.statement: The frill of Crittendenceratops features forward-curving, hook-like flanges along its central top portion.
facts.quote: Crittendenceratops is distinguished by forward-curving, hook-like flanges located along the central portion of the top of the frill

facts.statement: The frill exhibits a thickening in the parietal portion.
facts.quote: a thickening of the frill in the parietal portion

facts.statement: Dalman et al. (2018) classified Crittendenceratops within the tribe Nasutoceratopsini of the subfamily Centrosaurinae.
facts.quote: Crittendenceratops was assigned to the Nasutoceratopsini (which also includes Avaceratops, Nasutoceratops, and Yehuecauhceratops), a tribe of the ceratopsid subfamily Centrosaurinae, by Dalman et al. (2018).

facts.statement: Fossils of Crittendenceratops date from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)
